title: Trump Names Stephen Miller Chief of Staff; Wiles Moves to Political Operation
excerpt: President Donald Trump has named top aide Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles in the most significant White House person
content:
President Donald Trump has named top aide Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles in the most significant White House personnel move of his second term — days after Republicans suffered historic losses in the midterm elections.

Trump announced the change Friday, Nov. 6, in a post on Truth Social. Miller, 41, currently deputy chief of staff for policy and the president's homeland security adviser, will begin as chief of staff on Monday, Nov. 9. Wiles, 69, moves to the president's political operation.

“I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026,” Trump wrote. “Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation.”

Wiles confirmed Friday was her final day as chief of staff, posting on X: “Today is my last day as White House Chief of Staff.” Two sources familiar with the matter told CNN she submitted her resignation Thursday evening. Wiles was the nation's first female White House chief of staff, and she previously worked on Trump's three campaigns before being tapped for the role.

Why it matters for the border

Miller has been the architect of the president's hardline immigration agenda, and he has widened his portfolio over the past year to include wide swaths of domestic policy, advocating an expansive view of executive power, according to CNN. His elevation to the top staff position in the West Wing signals that the president does not intend to fundamentally change his governing approach, despite the midterm losses.

For Laredo and Webb County, the choice is not abstract. Immigration and border enforcement policy is set in the White House, and the chief of staff controls what reaches the president's desk. Miller's appointment comes as Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress, setting up a confrontation over immigration, tariffs, and health care in the final two years of Trump's term.

The overhaul follows Wiles becoming a target of Steve Bannon, Trump's former chief strategist, and other MAGA allies after Republicans lost control of the House and Senate, according to USA Today. The reshuffle also follows a series of resignations within the Department of Justice, including key figures Harmeet Dhillon and John Eisenberg.

Miller posted on X Friday: “It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have served on his team from Day One, and I am honored beyond words to serve as his White House Chief of Staff.”
